liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (5 reviews): Reviewer recalls Jerry giving everything on Morning Dew, with the crowd strongly into it; Reviewer believed Jerry looked teary-eyed during the final verse of Morning Dew, and found it deeply moving [12][13][18][19][20]
- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Shakedown features amusing punches in the mix, like a horn section; Reviewer usually dislikes Shakedowns with Vince, but considers this one worth hearing [15][16]
- **Foolish Heart** (2 reviews): Jerry has a nice moment near the end of the set-closing Foolish Heart, despite vocal recording issues; Reviewer calls the Foolish Heart vibrant and says Jerry played prettily that night [11][16]
- **Eyes Of The World** (2 reviews): Reviewer lists Eyes among the standout performances of the show; Reviewer especially loves the Eyes jam [15][20]
- **Corrina** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the longest Corrina jam they've heard, with Phil experimental and Jerry unwilling to stop [14]
- **Drums** (1 review): Pre-recorded digital drums from Mickey are used sparingly, and the end of Corrina into drums is surprisingly strong [17]
- **Space** (1 review): Reviewer found the drums and space segment quite trippy [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1992-05-24.119319.Sennheiser441.d5scott.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 18 songs; 147 min [1]
- **gd1992-05-24.150516.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 156 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd92-05-24.sbd.larson.8704.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 135 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer found the soundboard's vocals disappointing, especially Jerry's, with vocal problems in the recording; Sound resembles shows from a few days earlier, close to the 3/20 show, with faint hiss that disappears when turned up [11][14]
- **gd1992-05-24.sbd.miller.92272.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 156 min; rated 3.38/5 by 8 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended, sitting near the front of the lawn, and found the live sound disappointing compared with a Cal Expo show [11]
- Reviewer's second Dead show ever, after seeing the previous day's show [12]
- Reviewer saw Vince's keyboard appear to become a giant Mayan temple while dancing on Shoreline's steep lawn [16]
- Sound is compared to the 3/20 recording and to shows from a few days prior [14]
- Reviewer sees this show as a diamond in the rough among 1992 shows [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1992-05-24.119319.Sennheiser441.d5scott.flac16**: taped by D5scott; transferred by D5scott; source: Source: 2 Sennheiser 441 microphones > Sony TC-D5M - analog master cassettes; [1]
- **gd1992-05-24.150516.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  July 24, 2020; source: SBD > DAT Master (Panasonic SV-3700/48k) > Cassette Master (Tascam 122mkIII/TDK SA-X100) [2]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; no patches were needed because tape flips overlapped; files are 16-bit, 44.1 kHz [2]
- **gd92-05-24.sbd.larson.8704.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> MC> DAT> ZA2 (S/PDIF)> Wavelab3.03> SHN [9]
- **gd1992-05-24.sbd.miller.92272.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Dat -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Sameh Tawfik Grateful Dead: [1992-05-23 Shoreline Amphitheatre, Mountain View, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1992-05-23-shoreline-amphitheatre-mountain-view-ca-usa/) [23]
